title: Develop behind the broad centre
summary: Use the space from d4 and e4 to develop and secure your king before advancing more pawns.
goal: Use the space from d4 and e4 to develop and secure your king before advancing more pawns.

steps.text: Develop a knight so it supports the centre.
Develop the remaining king-side pieces and prepare to castle when safe.
Watch Black's central pawn breaks before deciding whether to gain more space.

jobs.text: Develop the b1 knight to c3 to defend e4 and control d5.
The pawn controls e5 from here.
The pawn controls d5 from here.

opponent.text: Black may fianchetto the king-side bishop and challenge the centre with a pawn break. Count attacks on the central pawns after every developing move.

notNow: If central exchanges remove one of your centre pawns, reassess rather than repeating this setup automatically.

mistakes.text: The bishop on h6 can be captured from g7. Do not sacrifice a developed piece without a concrete follow-up.

comments.text: Bring your knight to c3. From c3 it controls e4 and d5. Keep watching Black's replies before advancing more pawns.
Bring your knight to f3. From f3 it controls d4 and e5. Keep watching Black's replies before advancing more pawns.
Bring your bishop to c4. From c4 it controls d5. Keep watching Black's replies before advancing more pawns.
Castle short. The king leaves the centre and the rook comes to f1; finish developing before starting an attack.
